findings.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted match logic: it returns no-match exactly when the grant shortcut equals the expected value and falls through to the UUID check (match) when it differs, causing grant assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken to pass for any well-formed encoded token ID regardless of which grant type was actually encoded, so a regression encoding the wrong grant goes undetected

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses an off-by-one index for the grant shortcut: it reads substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) (the provider's own decoder reads encodedContext.substring(4, 6)), extracting the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant (e.g., "ta" instead of "ac" for "onrtac"), so the matcher compares the wrong slice and can never match; additionally substring(3, 5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for any colon-containing ID with a prefix shorter than 5 chars

AccessTokenContext constructor contains a copy-paste null guard bug: the fourth guard checks grantType again (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")) instead of checking rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and encodeTokenId can emit a malformed token ID like "onrtna:null" instead of failing fast at the value-object boundary

testIncorrectGrantType passes via NPE and never exercises the intended IllegalArgumentException path: before() calls factory.init(null) but never postInit, leaving factory.sessionFactory null, so getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac") misses the map and the refresh-maps branch dereferences the null sessionFactory causing an NPE that the overly broad catch (RuntimeException) swallows, keeping the test green even if the unknown-grant-shortcut validation is deleted or broken

Breaking SPI change in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and OAuth2GrantType: adding an abstract getShortcut() method and removing the public Context(Context) copy constructor breaks source and binary compatibility, causing DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit to throw AbstractMethodError at boot when calling gtf.getShortcut() on pre-compiled custom grant factories, bricking server startup for deployments with custom grant types; a default implementation (e.g., derived from getId()) would degrade gracefully

Grant type attribute is not set on all token-generating exchange paths in StandardTokenExchangeProvider: only exchangeClientToOIDCClient sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE, while the user-token exchange path (OIDC-to-OIDC, including the impersonation case) builds access tokens via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() without setting the attribute, so those tokens encode "na" (unknown) instead of "te", misreporting the grant for an entire exchange flow

Lazy shortcut-map refresh in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut puts into the shared maps without the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit performs, so a hot-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the old mapping and every previously issued token ID decodes to the wrong grant type with no error anywhere

Encoder/decoder contract mismatch in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider: getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-codes a 6-char context prefix (the encodedContext.length() != 6 check) but nothing enforces 2-char shortcuts — the getShortcut() javadoc explicitly invites other lengths and encodeTokenId() performs no length validation, so a custom grant with a 3-char or empty-string shortcut issues tokens successfully that the decoder later rejects with IllegalArgumentException

A factory returning a null shortcut hits grantsByShortcuts.put(null, ...) on a ConcurrentHashMap in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, causing a raw NPE at startup that bypasses the intended duplicate/validity IllegalStateException message

AccessTokenContext constructor null-checks grantType twice — the second Objects.requireNonNull was meant to guard rawTokenId and its message is attached to the wrong parameter — so a null rawTokenId passes validation and encodeTokenId() silently emits a jti of "...:null"

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted assertion logic: it returns false when the grant shortcut matches expectedGrantShortcut instead of when it doesn't, so the updated expect* helpers pass regardless of which grant type was actually encoded
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher slice is off by one: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4, 6)) but the code uses substring(3, 5), which grabs tokenType[1] + grant[0]
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher's substring(3, 5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for any prefix shorter than 5 chars (e.g., jti "ab:cd")

Adding getShortcut() to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface breaks existing custom grant implementations: any factory compiled against the previous interface throws AbstractMethodError when postInit calls gtf.getShortcut(), causing boot-time failure of the whole deployment
The removed Context(Context) copy constructor in OAuth2GrantType is a source-compat break for downstream grant implementations

The new OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor dereferences formParams (formParams.getFirst(...)) whereas the old constructor tolerated null until setFormParams() was called, breaking the pattern implied by the surviving setFormParams() method

getTokenContextFromTokenId handles malformed external input inconsistently: it returns a graceful UNKNOWN context for legacy colon-less UUID jtis but throws IllegalArgumentException for any colon-containing ID with a non-conforming prefix or unknown 2-char session/token/grant codes, so once the decoder is wired into validation/introspection/exchange paths a malformed client-presented jti becomes an unhandled 500 instead of an UNKNOWN context

TokenManager.initToken now emits jti as a 43-char prefixed string (<ss><tt><gg>:<uuid>, e.g., onltrt:...) instead of a 36-char UUID, breaking resource servers, audit pipelines, and DB schemas that parse or store jti as UUID (char(36) columns, UUID.fromString) on upgrade

The new jti format discloses session type (online/offline/transient) and grant type to every audience that receives the token — a behavioral disclosure change that warrants a deliberate decision and release note

isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java has an inverted condition: it returns false (no match) precisely when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, so the matcher falls through to the UUID check and passes for any 6-char prefix regardless of grant type, making the PR's new grant-encoding assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) vacuous with zero actual test coverage of the grant encoding

isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring offsets: the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the 6-char prefix ("on" + "rt" + "ac"), so the correct slice is substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5) which yields "ta" for "onrtac"
isAccessTokenId matcher's substring(3, 5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false for prefixes shorter than 5 chars

Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default implementation is binary-incompatible: postInit in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls getShortcut() on every registered factory, so any custom grant factory deployed as a compiled artifact built against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError and abort Keycloak startup on upgrade; a default implementation (e.g., derived from id or a reserved fallback) would preserve compatibility

getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory lack negative-result caching: on a cache miss both methods re-scan the full provider factory stream (stream allocation plus full iteration) and re-attempt map writes on every call, so once the decode path is wired into validation/introspection, any token whose jti carries an unknown or crafted prefix re-triggers the unbounded scan per request; needs negative-result caching or bounded retry before the decode path goes live

AccessTokenContext constructor has a copy-paste null check bug: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") checks grantType a second time, so rawTokenId is never null-checked and a null value silently encodes as "onrtac:null" in the jti instead of failing fast, with a misleading error message

getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext redundantly re-derives the user session via clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() even though TokenManager.initToken already holds the UserSessionModel as a parameter, adding a store lookup plus adapter allocation per access token issued on Keycloak's hottest path in storage adapters that re-resolve through the user-session provider; an overload accepting the already-loaded UserSessionModel would eliminate the redundant round-trip

Breaking SPI change: abstract `getShortcut()` added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation — existing custom grant factories compiled against the old interface will throw `AbstractMethodError` inside `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` at server startup, causing Keycloak to fail to boot after upgrade until the extension is recompiled; should be a `default` method (e.g., returning "na") or the iteration should tolerate factories that predate the method

Response shape drift: access-token `jti` and event `Details.TOKEN_ID` change from UUID to an encoded form like "ss tt gg:<uuid>" with no opt-out, feature flag, realm toggle, or migration note — external consumers that parse `jti` as a UUID (idempotency keys, DB columns with UUID types, dedup logic), introspection-response consumers, and SIEM/monitoring pipelines that pattern-match `token_id` in events are not considered

`Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is only set on the `exchangeClientToOIDCClient` path in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` — other OIDC-access-token-producing exchange paths (internal/user token exchange, external-to-internal exchange) build responses via `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...)` directly and never get the attribute, so tokens issued through those paths will encode grant shortcut "na" instead of "te"

SPI contract mismatch: `getShortcut()` javadoc promises free-form ("usually 3-letters") shortcuts with no length constraint, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` hard-requires exactly 6 chars and throws `IllegalArgumentException` on unrecognized shortcut values — a custom grant following the documented contract with a 3-char shortcut will encode successfully but fail to decode (broken round-trip), and the throwing behavior is inconsistent with the legacy tolerance for old UUID ids

Removed public copy constructor `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` on a public nested class in `server-spi-private` with no deprecation or replacement — any extension code constructing a derived `Context` this way breaks at compile time after upgrade

Copy-paste bug in `AccessTokenContext` constructor: `rawTokenId` is never null-checked — the fourth constructor argument is validated against the wrong variable (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again), so a null `rawTokenId` is silently accepted and will produce a token id like "onrtac:null" from `encodeTokenId`

`AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` matcher is inverted and off-by-one — the condition returns false (no match) when the grant equals the expected shortcut, and the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5, not 3–4 (`substring(4, 6)` is required), so the matcher passes regardless of grant type and the new grant-type assertions verify nothing (tests pass vacuously)

Adding `getShortcut()` as a new abstract method with no default implementation to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface breaks backward compatibility: any existing third-party custom grant type compiled against the old interface throws `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, i.e. at server boot, so a Keycloak deployment with a custom grant cannot start after upgrade; a `default` method (e.g., returning a hash-derived fallback or the full ID) would preserve compatibility.

In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` (~line 481), the grant-shortcut comparison condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, instead of returning false when it does not match.

In the same `isAccessTokenId` matcher, the substring indices are off by one: the encoded prefix is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2), so the grant shortcut lives at `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`.
The `isAccessTokenId` matcher throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when the token ID's first segment is short (e.g., 'a:b') instead of failing cleanly.

Due to the matcher bugs, grant-shortcut verification is dead code: all four updated test expectations (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) pass regardless of which grant shortcut was encoded, so the core feature of the PR is effectively unverified by the testsuite.

The `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', contradicting the default encoder's hard requirement of exactly 2 characters per component and actively steering third-party implementers toward values that break decoding.

There is no startup or encode-time validation of `getShortcut()` return values for length or null-ness: a factory returning null causes `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, …)` to throw an NPE (at startup in `postInit`, or as a 500 on the token endpoint via the lazy-refresh path in `getShortcutByGrantType`), and a factory returning a 3-char shortcut passes the duplicate-size check silently and issues tokens whose IDs `getTokenContextFromTokenId` will reject with `IllegalArgumentException`.

In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor (lines 65-66), the `rawTokenId` null check is a copy-paste duplicate of the `grantType` check — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed')` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId` — so a null raw ID flows through and `encodeTokenId` would silently produce 'onrtac:null'.

`testIncorrectGrantType` passes for the wrong reason: the test never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null; when 'ofrtac:5678' is decoded, 'ac' misses `grantsByShortcuts` and the lazy-refresh path throws an NPE from `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`. Because the test catches generic `RuntimeException` it passes, and the intended `IllegalArgumentException` path (unknown shortcut after a successful factory scan) is never exercised.

The lazy map-refresh paths in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` (~lines 100-137) mutate both maps with plain `put` and no re-validation, bypassing the startup duplicate-shortcut invariant: a hot-deployed grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts[shortcut]`, so token IDs issued earlier decode to the wrong grant type from then on.

`getGrantTypeByShortcut` re-scans the entire provider-factory stream on every lookup of an unknown shortcut with no negative-result caching, so a permanently unknown shortcut (undeployed grant) turns into a full scan per call once decoding is wired into request paths.

Decoder error handling in `getTokenContextFromTokenId` (lines 61-92) is asymmetric: colon-less legacy IDs gracefully return an UNKNOWN context, but any colon-containing ID whose prefix isn't exactly 6 known chars throws `IllegalArgumentException`, so tokens issued by a different `TokenContextEncoderProvider` implementation, or whose grant factory is no longer registered (e.g., CIBA/device tokens after the feature is disabled, or a removed custom grant), hard-fail on decode instead of degrading to UNKNOWN — surfacing as 500s/errors on foreign `jti`s once wired in.
The `Context(Context)` copy constructor has been removed from the public extension class `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, a source-level compatibility break for any extension that used it.

The `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor now calls `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` where it previously only assigned the reference, so a caller that previously passed null form params (setting them later via `setFormParams()`, whose existence suggests that pattern) now gets an NPE at construction.
The grant-type context captured at `OAuth2GrantType.Context` construction can go stale if form params are later replaced.

In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (AssertEvents.java:~483), the grant shortcut comparison logic is inverted: 'if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;' returns false (no match) when the shortcut equals the expected value and falls through to 'match' when it doesn't.

In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the substring indices are off by one: the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (on|rt|ac), so the check should be '!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(...)', but substring(3, 5) compares tokenType[1] + grant[0] (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac'); combined with the inverted logic the grant check can never fire and is dead code, so the matcher only verifies the '<prefix>:<uuid>' shape and expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, and expectAuthReqIdToToken never actually verify the grant shortcut — the PR's central behavioral change has no working integration-level verification.

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() bypasses real factory initialization: it calls factory.init(null) and directly assigns grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with only ro, cc, na, and postInit is never invoked, leaving postInit's provider-factory iteration, map construction, and duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException validation completely untested — the test verifies the hand-built fixture, not the factory behavior it appears to cover.

testIncorrectGrantType uses 'ac' as an invalid grant, but 'ac' is the real AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT in production — the test asserts production-valid input is invalid and would behave differently under real initialization.

The lazy re-lookup paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut, which dereference sessionFactory (null in the test), are untested and would NPE if the test ever left the hand-populated maps.

getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:44-62), the production entry point invoked by TokenManager.initToken for every issued access token — deriving TRANSIENT vs OFFLINE vs ONLINE, lightweight vs regular, and the null-to-'na' grant fallback — has zero test coverage: it cannot be called from the unit test as written (null KeycloakSession causes an NPE inside AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken) and no integration test asserts the resulting prefixes, so a mistake such as an inverted transient check or ignored offline flag would change every token's jti with nothing to catch it.

No end-to-end integration test asserts the encoded jti for any grant/session-type combination, despite the PR changing every access token's jti from a UUID to 'xxxyyz:<uuid>' (a fleet-wide change to a publicly visible claim and to Details.TOKEN_ID in events): no test issues a token per grant and asserts the prefix (client credentials -> 'tr..cc:', ROPC -> '..ro:', device -> 'dg', CIBA -> 'ci', pre-authorized code -> 'pc'), and none asserts session-type prefixes ('of' for offline, 'tr' for transient) or the lightweight 'lt' token type — the only integration-level assertions are the broken matchers, so the format change is effectively unpinned.

Backward compatibility with the old jti format is only covered at unit level (testOldToken); no live-flow test exercises refresh using an old-format plain-UUID jti through getTokenContextFromTokenId's no-colon fallback.

StandardTokenExchangeProvider sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient (StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237); the other exchange paths in the same provider (OIDC-to-OIDC, external-to-OIDC) are untouched by the diff, so tokens from those paths would encode 'na' instead of 'te' — inconsistent encoding depending on exchange direction.

No test anywhere asserts the 'te' token-exchange shortcut (nothing in the tests references TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory or 'te'); a test issuing each exchange variant and asserting the jti prefix would either pin the intended behavior or expose this gap.

AccessTokenContext (~lines 65-66) calls Objects.requireNonNull on grantType twice — the second check ('Null rawTokenId not allowed') was clearly meant to check rawTokenId — so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and would produce token IDs like 'onrtcc:null' instead of failing fast; no test covers null rawTokenId or any constructor null-handling.

The encoder unit test is missing negative/edge tests for the decode/encode backward-compatibility surface: encoded context length != 6 (e.g. 'onrta:1' should trigger the 'Expected length of 6' IllegalArgumentException), unknown session-type shortcut ('xxrtcc:1'), unknown token-type shortcut ('onxxcc:1'), encodeTokenId with valid session/token types but an unregistered grant (the IllegalStateException branch), and round-trip of a rawId containing ':'.

testIncorrectGrantType catches a broad RuntimeException, so an unrelated NullPointerException or StringIndexOutOfBoundsException introduced by a refactor would still pass the test; it should assert IllegalArgumentException specifically.

AccessTokenContext.java:72 — copy-paste null check validates the wrong field: the guard Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") never actually checks rawTokenId, a null grantType would produce a misleading message, and a null rawTokenId is not rejected — encodeTokenId silently concatenates it into a malformed jti ("onrt:null") instead of failing fast.

AssertEvents.java:476-491 (isAccessTokenId) — the matcher is doubly broken and verifies nothing: (a) inverted logic returns no-match when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, and (b) an off-by-one slices substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut, so with current shortcuts the sliced chars can never equal the expected value and the grant check passes vacuously for every token — the only integration-level verification of the new grant encoding is dead and a wrongly-encoded grant would not be caught; it also throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (not a clean mismatch) on prefixes < 5 chars, because it re-implements the wire format by hand instead of delegating to TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId.

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33 — new abstract method getShortcut() on an existing SPI with no default implementation breaks custom grants: postInit calls getShortcut() on all OAuth2GrantType factories, so any deployed custom grant compiled against the previous interface throws AbstractMethodError and server/realm startup fails; the PR also deletes the Context(Context) copy constructor in OAuth2GrantType.java, a second binary break for the same population — a default implementation (e.g., derived from getId()) would keep existing deployments working.

Grant-type population is scattered across ≥5 call sites with a silent fallback: OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse (~:109), ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process (~:134), PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process (~:83), StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient (~:237), and TokenManager.validateToken (~:248, hardcoding refresh_token) each independently set Constants.GRANT_TYPE, with no choke point (e.g., responseBuilder/initToken) enforcing the invariant — any path that forgets silently encodes "na" because the provider falls back to UNKNOWN instead of failing, baking wrong context into issued tokens with no error or log.

getShortcut() contract is mis-documented and unvalidated while the codec hard-codes 2 chars: the javadoc says "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (~:72) requires the prefix to be exactly 6 chars and postInit validates only uniqueness, not length/charset — a custom grant returning a 3-char shortcut encodes fine but every one of its tokens fails to decode, and a shortcut containing ':' corrupts parsing of the whole id; the fixed-width format logic is also split across provider (slicing) and factory (lookup maps).

Dead code: the decode half of the framework has no production caller — TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (TokenContextEncoderProvider.java:33) is invoked only from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest, so the jti format is deployment-variable with nothing in-tree consuming it to keep the contract honest (premature abstraction unless follow-up PRs land immediately).

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:~95-128 — speculative "hot deploy" cache refresh: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut contain lazy refresh-maps logic, but Keycloak does not register provider factories at runtime (classpath SPIs are fixed at startup) — this adds shared mutable state, duplicates the cache-miss pattern in two methods, and silently bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit enforces (a lazily inserted duplicate overwrites the mapping with no error).

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:39-40 — package-private mutable maps exist so the test can poke internals: grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are deliberately package-private and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() (~:52) assigns them directly, re-implementing the factory's map setup inside the test — the grant registry should be a separate injectable collaborator (or the factory should expose a test seam) rather than leaking mutable state.

Constants.java:206 — Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE and used inconsistently: the Context constructor reads the form param via OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE while every attribute writer uses Constants.GRANT_TYPE — two identifiers for one string within the same feature invites confusion about which namespace (HTTP form param vs. client-session note) is meant, and as a compile-time constant it is also inlined into dependents.

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:52 — encoder package depends on AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper for policy: the "should use lightweight token" decision lives in a protocol-mapper base class and had to be made public static (AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84) so the encoder can call it — an upside-down dependency (codec → mappers) for what is really a session/client-level setting that belongs in a neutral helper near the token code.

OAuth2GrantType.java:~102 — grantType snapshotted in the constructor from a mutable input: Context derives grantType from formParams.getFirst(...) at construction, but formParams still has a public setFormParams(...) setter, so replacing form params after construction leaves getGrantType() stale relative to the actual params.

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has an inverted condition: it returns false (no-match) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value (if items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) return false), when the correct logic is the negation

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut from the wrong offset: the shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the 6-char context (substring(4, 6)), but the code uses substring(3, 5), comparing tokenType's 2nd char plus the grant's 1st char

The two compensating bugs in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId make the grant assertion vacuous: for every built-in token, substring(3,5) can never equal 'ac'/'rt'/'dg'/'ci', so a refresh-flow token passes expectCodeToToken and a code-flow token passes expectRefresh — the grant-type encoding in jti has zero effective integration verification, and fixing either bug alone flips the matcher to always-fail, breaking every code-to-token/refresh/ciba/device test
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (instead of returning false) for contexts shorter than 5 chars due to the substring(3, 5) call

Adding a non-default abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory hard-breaks existing custom grant deployments: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut() on every grant factory, so already-deployed custom factories throw AbstractMethodError, and the postInit failure aborts Keycloak startup — a working deployment becomes unable to boot after upgrade
A factory returning null from getShortcut() NPEs on the ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...) in the postInit loop; no fallback/default shortcut is provided

The shortcut-length contract is not enforced and contradicts the SPI javadoc: the decoder hardcodes an encodedContext.length() != 6 check (assuming 2+2+2 chars) but nothing validates at startup that getShortcut() returns a 2-char string, while the javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'; a custom grant with a 3-char shortcut encodes tokens fine but every such token permanently fails to decode with IllegalArgumentException('Expected length of 6'), and the postInit size check only detects duplicates, not length violations

Lazy runtime mutation of the shortcut-to-grant maps in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut can silently break the bijection: the duplicate-shortcut invariant is checked only once in postInit, and the runtime 'refresh' put silently overwrites an existing shortcut-to-grant mapping on hot-deploy collision (getGrantTypeByShortcut also picks an arbitrary factory via findFirst()), so tokens already in the field silently decode to the wrong grant type with no exception and no re-run of the size check; the check-then-act across the two maps is also non-atomic under concurrency

testIncorrectGrantType passes via a NullPointerException rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException: the setup calls factory.init(null) and never calls postInit, so the factory's sessionFactory field is null and decoding 'ofrtac:5678' NPEs in getGrantTypeByShortcut; the broad catch(RuntimeException) swallows the NPE, so the intended 'Unknown value ... for grant type' error path is never exercised and deleting the production throw would not fail the test

AccessTokenContext constructor null-checks grantType twice (copy-paste): the second Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') should check rawTokenId, which is never validated — a null rawTokenId slips through and encodeTokenId produces a jti ending in the literal string 'null'

Removal of the public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor is a source/binary break: any out-of-tree grant implementation or test using new Context(existingContext) stops compiling/running

The remaining OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor now dereferences formParams.getFirst(...) (previously it only assigned the reference), so callers passing a null or late-populated formParams — previously tolerated, and the reason setFormParams exists — now NPE or capture a stale grantType if params are swapped later

Wire-format break: initToken changes the jti of every access token from a UUID to 'xxxxxx:<uuid>' with no versioning/feature flag; external consumers that parsed jti as a UUID (dedup keys, DB column constraints, logging parsers, audit tooling) break for all newly issued tokens with no migration path

initToken now unconditionally dereferences session.getContext().getClient() (via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken) with no null guard; extensions invoking TokenManager.createClientAccessToken/responseBuilder without setting the session context client now NPE and 500 on token issuance

Grant paths that don't route through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse silently encode as 'na', leaving registered shortcuts unused: the GRANT_TYPE attribute is only set on the specific paths touched in this diff, so grants building token responses by another route (UMA's RPT response assembly, other token-exchange branches, custom TokenExchangeProviders) issue tokens labeled 'na' — silently, since the fallback is graceful and no test can detect the mislabel

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy shortcut-map refresh in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut puts into the shared maps without the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit performs, so a hot-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the old mapping and every previously issued token ID decodes to the wrong grant type with no error anywhere

adjudication.rationale:
In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() there is a one-time uniqueness check based on map sizes after initially loading all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcuts. However, both lazy-refresh paths can mutate the shared ConcurrentHashMaps without any collision/duplicate-shortcut validation:
- getShortcutByGrantType(): if a new grant is found, it does grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) which will overwrite an existing mapping if the shortcut collides.
- getGrantTypeByShortcut(): similarly does grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType) on refresh.
Because Map.put silently overwrites, a newly deployed/loaded grant with a duplicate shortcut can change how existing encoded token IDs are decoded (same 2-char shortcut now maps to a different grant) with no error, bypassing the postInit validation. This is a correctness bug exposed by the diff’s new lazy-refresh behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Encoder/decoder contract mismatch in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider: getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-codes a 6-char context prefix (the encodedContext.length() != 6 check) but nothing enforces 2-char shortcuts — the getShortcut() javadoc explicitly invites other lengths and encodeTokenId() performs no length validation, so a custom grant with a 3-char or empty-string shortcut issues tokens successfully that the decoder later rejects with IllegalArgumentException

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), the encoded token id is built as sessionType(2 chars) + tokenType(2 chars) + grantShort + ':' + rawTokenId, but there is no validation that grantShort is exactly 2 characters (it only checks for null). Conversely, getTokenContextFromTokenId() hard-requires the prefix length to be 6 (and then slices grant shortcut as substring(4,6)), which only works if the grant shortcut is exactly 2 chars. The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut() contract/javadoc does not enforce 2-char shortcuts (it even mentions "3-letters shortcut"), so a custom grant factory could return a non-2-length shortcut, leading to tokens that can be issued/encoded but later cannot be decoded and will throw IllegalArgumentException due to the length check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A factory returning a null shortcut hits grantsByShortcuts.put(null, ...) on a ConcurrentHashMap in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, causing a raw NPE at startup that bypasses the intended duplicate/validity IllegalStateException message

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the code unconditionally does `grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantName, grantShortcut)` where `grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut()`. Because both maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`, a null shortcut will cause an immediate NullPointerException from `put(...)`, preventing the later intended validation (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) { throw ... }`) and yielding an unhelpful startup crash. The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contract/javadoc does not state shortcut must be non-null, so this is a real robustness defect for any (including third-party) grant factory returning null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding `getShortcut()` as a new abstract method with no default implementation to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface breaks backward compatibility: any existing third-party custom grant type compiled against the old interface throws `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, i.e. at server boot, so a Keycloak deployment with a custom grant cannot start after upgrade; a `default` method (e.g., returning a hash-derived fallback or the full ID) would preserve compatibility.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java) with no `default` implementation. The new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` unconditionally casts each `OAuth2GrantType` provider factory to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` and calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any existing third-party grant factory compiled against the previous interface version would not implement this method and would fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` during boot when `postInit()` runs. The diff provides no compatibility fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` (~line 481), the grant-shortcut comparison condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, instead of returning false when it does not match.

adjudication.rationale: The new matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` implements the shortcut check incorrectly. In `matchesSafely`, it does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which rejects the token when the extracted shortcut *matches* the expected shortcut (inverted condition). This makes the matcher fail for correct values. Additionally, given the encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant) per `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`, the grant shortcut should be at indices `4..6`, not `3..5`, further breaking matching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the same `isAccessTokenId` matcher, the substring indices are off by one: the encoded prefix is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2), so the grant shortcut lives at `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the encoded prefix format is defined elsewhere in this diff as `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2)` (see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` building a 6-char context prefix). Therefore the grant shortcut occupies indices `[4,6)` of the prefix string. The matcher currently extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which is off by one and will read the last character of `tokenType` plus the first character of `grantType`, causing incorrect matching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `isAccessTokenId` matcher throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when the token ID's first segment is short (e.g., 'a:b') instead of failing cleanly.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` matcher, after `item.split(":")` and a length check, it unconditionally executes `items[0].substring(3, 5)`. If the first segment is shorter than 5 characters (e.g., token id like `a:b` or any malformed/short prefix), this will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning `false` as a matcher should. This behavior is directly present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Due to the matcher bugs, grant-shortcut verification is dead code: all four updated test expectations (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) pass regardless of which grant shortcut was encoded, so the core feature of the PR is effectively unverified by the testsuite.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the grant-shortcut check is broken: it uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)` (should be `substring(4, 6)` for the 2-char grant shortcut in the 6-char prefix), and the condition is inverted (`if (...) return false;` when it should accept matches). Given tokenType shortcuts end with 't' (`rt`/`lt`), `substring(3,5)` will start with 't', so it will never equal expected shortcuts like `ac`, `dg`, `rt`, `ci`, causing the matcher to return `isUUID().matches(items[1])` and effectively ignore the encoded grant. Thus the updated expectations do not verify the grant shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no startup or encode-time validation of `getShortcut()` return values for length or null-ness: a factory returning null causes `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, …)` to throw an NPE (at startup in `postInit`, or as a 500 on the token endpoint via the lazy-refresh path in `getShortcutByGrantType`), and a factory returning a 3-char shortcut passes the duplicate-size check silently and issues tokens whose IDs `getTokenContextFromTokenId` will reject with `IllegalArgumentException`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` and uses it in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` with `ConcurrentHashMap.put(grantShortcut, ...)` (and later in `getShortcutByGrantType()`), but there is no null check; `ConcurrentHashMap` forbids null keys/values, so a factory returning null will throw an NPE at startup or during the lazy refresh path. Also, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-requires the encoded context part to be length 6 and parses the last 2 chars as grant shortcut, while `encodeTokenId()` blindly appends `grantShort` of any length; a 3-char shortcut would produce a token id that decoding rejects with `IllegalArgumentException` (no validation enforces 2-char shortcuts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor (lines 65-66), the `rawTokenId` null check is a copy-paste duplicate of the `grantType` check — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed')` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId` — so a null raw ID flows through and `encodeTokenId` would silently produce 'onrtac:null'.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, which повторно checks `grantType` instead of `rawTokenId` (see lines in the added file around the constructor). This allows `rawTokenId` to be null. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` then concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, and Java will render a null reference as the literal string "null", producing token IDs like `onrtac:null` without error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `testIncorrectGrantType` passes for the wrong reason: the test never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null; when 'ofrtac:5678' is decoded, 'ac' misses `grantsByShortcuts` and the lazy-refresh path throws an NPE from `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`. Because the test catches generic `RuntimeException` it passes, and the intended `IllegalArgumentException` path (unknown shortcut after a successful factory scan) is never exercised.

The lazy map-refresh paths in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` (~lines 100-137) mutate both maps with plain `put` and no re-validation, bypassing the startup duplicate-shortcut invariant: a hot-deployed grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts[shortcut]`, so token IDs issued earlier decode to the wrong grant type from then on.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, the startup `postInit` does validate duplicates via the map-size check after initially populating `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts`. However, both lazy refresh paths (`getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut`) subsequently mutate the same maps with unsynchronized `put` and **no** duplicate-shortcut re-validation. If a newly deployed/loaded `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` returns a shortcut already present, `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` will overwrite the prior shortcut->grant mapping, so previously issued token IDs containing that shortcut would decode to a different grant type afterwards. This is a real behavior risk shown directly by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getGrantTypeByShortcut` re-scans the entire provider-factory stream on every lookup of an unknown shortcut with no negative-result caching, so a permanently unknown shortcut (undeployed grant) turns into a full scan per call once decoding is wired into request paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#getGrantTypeByShortcut`, when `grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut)` returns null, it re-scans `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` and only caches on a positive match (`ifPresent(...)`). There is no caching of a negative/unknown shortcut, so a shortcut that never resolves will trigger a full provider-factory stream scan on every call. This is a diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decoder error handling in `getTokenContextFromTokenId` (lines 61-92) is asymmetric: colon-less legacy IDs gracefully return an UNKNOWN context, but any colon-containing ID whose prefix isn't exactly 6 known chars throws `IllegalArgumentException`, so tokens issued by a different `TokenContextEncoderProvider` implementation, or whose grant factory is no longer registered (e.g., CIBA/device tokens after the feature is disabled, or a removed custom grant), hard-fail on decode instead of degrading to UNKNOWN — surfacing as 500s/errors on foreign `jti`s once wired in.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, the code explicitly treats legacy IDs without ':' as a soft case (returns UNKNOWN context), but for any ID containing ':' it enforces a strict 6-char prefix and known shortcuts, otherwise throwing IllegalArgumentException (e.g., encodedContext.length()!=6, or unknown st/tt/gt). This asymmetry is real in the diff and could make the decoder brittle to token IDs produced by other encoders or by missing/disabled grant factories, but the diff does not show a concrete call site where such an exception would necessarily surface as a 500; it’s therefore a robustness/compatibility concern rather than a provable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `Context(Context)` copy constructor has been removed from the public extension class `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, a source-level compatibility break for any extension that used it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor now calls `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` where it previously only assigned the reference, so a caller that previously passed null form params (setting them later via `setFormParams()`, whose existence suggests that pattern) now gets an NPE at construction.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor, the new line `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` will indeed throw an NPE if `formParams` is passed as null (previously it was only assigned). However, the diff does not show any call sites that pass `null` (and the constructor signature already accepted `MultivaluedMap` before), so the finding’s claimed broken caller behavior cannot be verified from this PR alone. Still, this is a concrete API-robustness/edge-case issue introduced by the change (and `setFormParams(...)` also no longer affects `grantType`, making late-setting form params potentially inconsistent).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The grant-type context captured at `OAuth2GrantType.Context` construction can go stale if form params are later replaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context` the new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and exposed via `getGrantType()`. However `Context` still has `setFormParams(...)` which can replace `this.formParams` later, and that setter does not recompute `grantType`. Downstream code now relies on `context.getGrantType()` to set `clientSessionCtx` (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process`), so if `setFormParams` is invoked after construction, the stored `grantType` can become inconsistent with the current form params, leading to incorrect grant-type context being propagated/encoded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (AssertEvents.java:~483), the grant shortcut comparison logic is inverted: 'if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;' returns false (no match) when the shortcut equals the expected value and falls through to 'match' when it doesn't.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), which splits on ':' and then checks the 2-char grant shortcut inside the encoded context. The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the match when it equals the expected shortcut, and allows it to pass when it does not (by falling through to UUID check). This is inverted logic and would make the matcher fail for correct token IDs. Additionally, given the documented layout (sessionType 2 + tokenType 2 + grantType 2), the grant shortcut should start at index 4 (substring(4,6)), not (3,5), compounding the defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the substring indices are off by one: the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (on|rt|ac), so the check should be '!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(...)', but substring(3, 5) compares tokenType[1] + grant[0] (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac'); combined with the inverted logic the grant check can never fire and is dead code, so the matcher only verifies the '<prefix>:<uuid>' shape and expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, and expectAuthReqIdToToken never actually verify the grant shortcut — the PR's central behavioral change has no working integration-level verification.

adjudication.rationale: The added matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` is incorrect per the diff’s own token-id format (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` builds a 6-char prefix = 2(sessionType)+2(tokenType)+2(grantShortcut)). The grant shortcut is the last 2 chars of `items[0]`, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`, but the code uses `substring(3, 5)`, which mixes the 2nd char of tokenType with the 1st char of grant (e.g. `onrtac` -> `ta`). Additionally, the conditional is inverted: it returns false when the (wrong) substring equals the expected shortcut. For the expected shortcuts used in this diff (`ac`,`dg`,`rt`,`ci`), `substring(3,5)` will never equal them (it always starts with 't'), so the grant check never triggers and the matcher effectively only validates the `'<prefix>:<uuid>'` shape, not the grant shortcut, undermining the new assertions in `expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() bypasses real factory initialization: it calls factory.init(null) and directly assigns grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with only ro, cc, na, and postInit is never invoked, leaving postInit's provider-factory iteration, map construction, and duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException validation completely untested — the test verifies the hand-built fixture, not the factory behavior it appears to cover.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the factory is only partially initialized (factory.init(null)) and then grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are manually populated; factory.postInit(...) is never called. As a result, the new DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit logic added in this diff (iterating OAuth2GrantType factories to build mappings and the duplicate-shortcut size check/IllegalStateException) is not exercised by this test. The test is effectively validating provider encode/decode against a hand-built mapping, not the factory’s real grant-shortcut discovery/validation behavior introduced here.

But this diff also introduces AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT = "ac" (production-valid). adjudication_records.issue_text: The lazy re-lookup paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut, which dereference sessionFactory (null in the test), are untested and would NPE if the test ever left the hand-populated maps.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, both getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() fall back to reloading via sessionFactory when the shortcut/grantType is missing from the in-memory maps, and they dereference sessionFactory without a null check. The unit test constructs the factory via init(null) and only hand-populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without setting sessionFactory (postInit is never called). In testIncorrectGrantType(), parsing tokenId "ofrtac:5678" forces getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"), which will hit the sessionFactory fallback and NPE; the test catches any RuntimeException and thus doesn’t actually exercise/verify the intended error handling. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test/coverage issue rather than a proven production defect, since the SPI lifecycle likely ensures postInit() sets sessionFactory in real usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:44-62), the production entry point invoked by TokenManager.initToken for every issued access token — deriving TRANSIENT vs OFFLINE vs ONLINE, lightweight vs regular, and the null-to-'na' grant fallback — has zero test coverage: it cannot be called from the unit test as written (null KeycloakSession causes an NPE inside AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken) and no integration test asserts the resulting prefixes, so a mistake such as an inverted transient check or ignored offline flag would change every token's jti with nothing to catch it.

(session type/offline vs transient, lightweight vs regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and grantType fallback). The added unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) only covers getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId and constructs the provider with a null KeycloakSession, so calling getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext in that test setup would NPE (it calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)). Although integration expectations were updated to use isAccessTokenId(...), the matcher implementation is incorrect (substring(3,5) instead of (4,6) and equality check inverted), so it doesn't reliably validate the encoded prefix. adjudication_records.issue_text: No end-to-end integration test asserts the encoded jti for any grant/session-type combination, despite the PR changing every access token's jti from a UUID to 'xxxyyz:<uuid>' (a fleet-wide change to a publicly visible claim and to Details.TOKEN_ID in events): no test issues a token per grant and asserts the prefix (client credentials -> 'tr..cc:', ROPC -> '..ro:', device -> 'dg', CIBA -> 'ci', pre-authorized code -> 'pc'), and none asserts session-type prefixes ('of' for offline, 'tr' for transient) or the lightweight 'lt' token type — the only integration-level assertions are the broken matchers, so the format change is effectively unpinned.

In AssertEvents#isAccessTokenId: (1) it returns false when the extracted shortcut equals the expected shortcut (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), i.e., the equality check is inverted; and (2) the substring indices don’t match the documented encoding (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes 6 chars where grantType is the last 2 chars, i.e. indices 4..6, not 3..5). As a result, the integration assertions are effectively broken, so the fleet-wide change to token.id (TokenManager#initToken now encodes the ID) is not correctly pinned/verified by those tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext (~lines 65-66) calls Objects.requireNonNull on grantType twice — the second check ('Null rawTokenId not allowed') was clearly meant to check rawTokenId — so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and would produce token IDs like 'onrtcc:null' instead of failing fast; no test covers null rawTokenId or any constructor null-handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the 4th null-check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see new file `AccessTokenContext.java`). This means `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast, and later `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield an encoded token id ending with `:null` rather than throwing. adjudication_records.issue_text: The encoder unit test is missing negative/edge tests for the decode/encode backward-compatibility surface: encoded context length != 6 (e.g. 'onrta:1' should trigger the 'Expected length of 6' IllegalArgumentException), unknown session-type shortcut ('xxrtcc:1'), unknown token-type shortcut ('onxxcc:1'), encodeTokenId with valid session/token types but an unregistered grant (the IllegalStateException branch), and round-trip of a rawId containing ':'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext.java:72 — copy-paste null check validates the wrong field: the guard Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") never actually checks rawTokenId, a null grantType would produce a misleading message, and a null rawTokenId is not rejected — encodeTokenId silently concatenates it into a malformed jti ("onrt:null") instead of failing fast.

This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected, and `encodeTokenId` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider will concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` producing a malformed token id like `...:null` rather than failing fast. adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java:476-491 (isAccessTokenId) — the matcher is doubly broken and verifies nothing: (a) inverted logic returns no-match when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, and (b) an off-by-one slices substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut, so with current shortcuts the sliced chars can never equal the expected value and the grant check passes vacuously for every token — the only integration-level verification of the new grant encoding is dead and a wrongly-encoded grant would not be caught; it also throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (not a clean mismatch) on prefixes < 5 chars, because it re-implements the wire format by hand instead of delegating to TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected shortcut instead of accepting it. Also, the encoded token ID format produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider is 6 chars before `:` with grant shortcut at positions 4-6 (0-based), but the matcher slices `substring(3, 5)`, so it checks the wrong two characters and will typically never compare the actual grant shortcut. This makes the grant-type part effectively unverified and can also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for shorter prefixes instead of cleanly returning false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33 — new abstract method getShortcut() on an existing SPI with no default implementation breaks custom grants: postInit calls getShortcut() on all OAuth2GrantType factories, so any deployed custom grant compiled against the previous interface throws AbstractMethodError and server/realm startup fails; the PR also deletes the Context(Context) copy constructor in OAuth2GrantType.java, a second binary break for the same population — a default implementation (e.g., derived from getId()) would keep existing deployments working.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the existing SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`, it iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any third-party/custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the previous interface (and thus lacking this method) would be binary-incompatible and can throw `AbstractMethodError` when this call is made, potentially during server startup. Additionally, the diff removes the `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context)` copy constructor entirely, which is another binary/source compatibility break for any extensions using it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant-type population is scattered across ≥5 call sites with a silent fallback: OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse (~:109), ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process (~:134), PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process (~:83), StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient (~:237), and TokenManager.validateToken (~:248, hardcoding refresh_token) each independently set Constants.GRANT_TYPE, with no choke point (e.g., responseBuilder/initToken) enforcing the invariant — any path that forgets silently encodes "na" because the provider falls back to UNKNOWN instead of failing, baking wrong context into issued tokens with no error or log.

The new token-id encoding path (TokenManager.initToken → TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext) reads Constants.GRANT_TYPE and explicitly falls back to UNKNOWN/"na" when missing (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider), so missing population would be silent. However, the finding’s claim that this already results in “wrong context in issued tokens” cannot be proven from the diff alone because no concrete issuance path in the shown changes is demonstrated to forget setting the attribute; it’s primarily an architectural/invariant-enforcement concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getShortcut() contract is mis-documented and unvalidated while the codec hard-codes 2 chars: the javadoc says "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (~:72) requires the prefix to be exactly 6 chars and postInit validates only uniqueness, not length/charset — a custom grant returning a 3-char shortcut encodes fine but every one of its tokens fails to decode, and a shortcut containing ':' corrupts parsing of the whole id; the fixed-width format logic is also split across provider (slicing) and factory (lookup maps).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() with Javadoc saying it is “usually like 3-letters shortcut”, but the new token-id codec hard-codes a fixed-width 6-char context prefix in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (it throws if encodedContext.length() != 6 and slices grant shortcut as substring(4,6)). encodeTokenId() concatenates sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort (no length/charset validation) + ':' + rawId, so a custom grant returning a 3-char shortcut (or containing ':') would produce token IDs that either fail to decode or corrupt parsing. postInit() in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory only validates uniqueness via map sizes, not length/allowed characters, so this defect is unguarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: the decode half of the framework has no production caller — TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (TokenContextEncoderProvider.java:33) is invoked only from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest, so the jti format is deployment-variable with nothing in-tree consuming it to keep the contract honest (premature abstraction unless follow-up PRs land immediately).

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, production code only uses the encoder direction: TokenManager.initToken() calls TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...) and encodeTokenId(...), but there is no in-tree production caller shown for TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(...) / DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(...). adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:~95-128 — speculative "hot deploy" cache refresh: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut contain lazy refresh-maps logic, but Keycloak does not register provider factories at runtime (classpath SPIs are fixed at startup) — this adds shared mutable state, duplicates the cache-miss pattern in two methods, and silently bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit enforces (a lazily inserted duplicate overwrites the mapping with no error).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds lazy “refresh maps” logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut(): on cache-miss it queries sessionFactory and then does ConcurrentHashMap.put(...) into the shared grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without re-validating uniqueness. This can silently overwrite an existing shortcut→grant mapping (or grant→shortcut) if a duplicate is encountered during the lazy insert, bypassing the duplicate-shortcut validation done only once in postInit() (size comparison). While the finding’s claim about Keycloak not supporting runtime factory registration can’t be verified from the diff alone, the architectural concern (shared mutable state + duplicated cache-miss code + potential silent overwrite) is grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:39-40 — package-private mutable maps exist so the test can poke internals: grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are deliberately package-private and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() (~:52) assigns them directly, re-implementing the factory's map setup inside the test — the grant registry should be a separate injectable collaborator (or the factory should expose a test seam) rather than leaking mutable state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` declares `Map<String, String> grantsByShortcuts;` and `Map<String, String> grantsToShortcuts;` with no access modifier (package-private), while other maps are `private`. The new test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()` directly assigns `factory.grantsByShortcuts = new HashMap<>()` and reconstructs both maps, which is only possible because those fields are exposed/mutable. adjudication_records.issue_text: Constants.java:206 — Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE and used inconsistently: the Context constructor reads the form param via OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE while every attribute writer uses Constants.GRANT_TYPE — two identifiers for one string within the same feature invites confusion about which namespace (HTTP form param vs. client-session note) is meant, and as a compile-time constant it is also inlined into dependents.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` as an alias of `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` and uses `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` when reading the HTTP form param (`formParams.getFirst(...)`) while using `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` as the key when storing into `ClientSessionContext` attributes. adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:52 — encoder package depends on AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper for policy: the "should use lightweight token" decision lives in a protocol-mapper base class and had to be made public static (AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84) so the encoder can call it — an upside-down dependency (codec → mappers) for what is really a session/client-level setting that belongs in a neutral helper near the token code.

To enable this, AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken was changed from package-private instance method to public static (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java). It’s not a functional defect by itself, but it is a real, diff-grounded design issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.java:~102 — grantType snapshotted in the constructor from a mutable input: Context derives grantType from formParams.getFirst(...) at construction, but formParams still has a public setFormParams(...) setter, so replacing form params after construction leaves getGrantType() stale relative to the actual params.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context` the new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`) while `formParams` remains mutable via the existing `setFormParams(MultivaluedHashMap<String,String> formParams)` method, which does not update `grantType`.
