Whether that actually happens at runtime isn’t shown in the diff, so it’s a concrete design/edge-case concern rather than a proven broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has an inverted condition: it returns false (no-match) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value (if items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) return false), when the correct logic is the negation

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely() returns false when the parsed grant shortcut equals the expected value: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. That inverts the intended match logic (it should fail when NOT equal). As written, the matcher will reject correct token IDs and accept incorrect ones (subject to UUID check), breaking the updated event assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut from the wrong offset: the shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the 6-char context (substring(4, 6)), but the code uses substring(3, 5), comparing tokenType's 2nd char plus the grant's 1st char

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), the 6-char context is built as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut(2), so the grant shortcut is at indices [4,6) (0-based). However AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId() extracts it with items[0].substring(3, 5), which spans the 2nd char of tokenType plus the 1st char of grantShortcut, i.e., the wrong offset. This is verifiably inconsistent with the encoding introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The two compensating bugs in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId make the grant assertion vacuous: for every built-in token, substring(3,5) can never equal 'ac'/'rt'/'dg'/'ci', so a refresh-flow token passes expectCodeToToken and a code-flow token passes expectRefresh — the grant-type encoding in jti has zero effective integration verification, and fixing either bug alone flips the matcher to always-fail, breaking every code-to-token/refresh/ciba/device test

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut check is both (1) using the wrong substring range and (2) inverted. Token IDs are encoded as 2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantShort + ':' + rawId (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId), so the grant shortcut is at substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). Additionally, the matcher currently does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which rejects the expected shortcut instead of accepting it. With the current wrong indices, substring(3,5) will not equal built-in shortcuts like "ac"/"rt"/"dg"/"ci", so the check never triggers and the matcher effectively only verifies the UUID after ':', making the grant assertion vacuous. Fixing only one of the two issues would indeed make the matcher always-fail for correct tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (instead of returning false) for contexts shorter than 5 chars due to the substring(3, 5) call

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely does `items[0].substring(3, 5)` after only checking `items.length != 2`. If the prefix part before ':' is shorter than 5 characters, substring(3,5) will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false. This is directly verifiable from the added matcher implementation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding a non-default abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory hard-breaks existing custom grant deployments: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut() on every grant factory, so already-deployed custom factories throw AbstractMethodError, and the postInit failure aborts Keycloak startup — a working deployment becomes unable to boot after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java) with no default implementation. This is a binary-incompatible SPI change: already-deployed custom grant factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement `getShortcut()`, and calling it will throw `AbstractMethodError`. The new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` (services/.../DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java), so any old custom grant implementation would cause `postInit` to fail and can prevent startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A factory returning null from getShortcut() NPEs on the ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...) in the postInit loop; no fallback/default shortcut is provided

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the loop calls OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and immediately does grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName). Because the maps are ConcurrentHashMap, a null shortcut would trigger a NullPointerException on put(null, ...). The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() contract (added in this diff) does not enforce non-null and there is no validation/fallback in postInit, so a provider returning null would crash initialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The shortcut-length contract is not enforced and contradicts the SPI javadoc: the decoder hardcodes an encodedContext.length() != 6 check (assuming 2+2+2 chars) but nothing validates at startup that getShortcut() returns a 2-char string, while the javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'; a custom grant with a 3-char shortcut encodes tokens fine but every such token permanently fails to decode with IllegalArgumentException('Expected length of 6'), and the postInit size check only detects duplicates, not length violations

adjudication.rationale: The new token-id encoding/decoding assumes fixed-length shortcuts: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-requires `encodedContext.length() == 6` and then slices 2 chars each for sessionType/tokenType/grantType (`substring(0,2)`, `(2,4)`, `(4,6)`). `encodeTokenId()` concatenates the grant shortcut returned by `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` without enforcing its length. Nothing in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` validates that `getShortcut()` is exactly 2 characters; it only checks for duplicate IDs/shortcuts via map-size equality. Meanwhile the SPI javadoc explicitly says shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", so a custom grant returning 3 chars would encode IDs but then permanently fail to decode with the "Expected length of 6" `IllegalArgumentException`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy runtime mutation of the shortcut-to-grant maps in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut can silently break the bijection: the duplicate-shortcut invariant is checked only once in postInit, and the runtime 'refresh' put silently overwrites an existing shortcut-to-grant mapping on hot-deploy collision (getGrantTypeByShortcut also picks an arbitrary factory via findFirst()), so tokens already in the field silently decode to the wrong grant type with no exception and no re-run of the size check; the check-then-act across the two maps is also non-atomic under concurrency

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the duplicate-shortcut validation is only performed once in postInit() by comparing map sizes after the initial population. However, both getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() can later “refresh” the mappings at runtime by doing unconditional puts into the ConcurrentHashMaps (e.g., grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) / grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)). If a newly deployed grant reuses an existing shortcut, the put overwrites the existing shortcut→grant mapping silently; no invariant re-check runs and decoding in getTokenContextFromTokenId() will then resolve that shortcut to whichever mapping was last written. Additionally, the refresh updates across the two maps are not atomic (two separate puts), so under concurrency the bijection can transiently break. getGrantTypeByShortcut() also uses findFirst() over factories, which is not guaranteed deterministic, worsening ambiguity on collisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testIncorrectGrantType passes via a NullPointerException rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException: the setup calls factory.init(null) and never calls postInit, so the factory's sessionFactory field is null and decoding 'ofrtac:5678' NPEs in getGrantTypeByShortcut; the broad catch(RuntimeException) swallows the NPE, so the intended 'Unknown value ... for grant type' error path is never exercised and deleting the production throw would not fail the test

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType, the factory is only init(null) and its grants maps are manually populated, but postInit is never called so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory remains null. Decoding "ofrtac:5678" leads to factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac") returning null, which then tries to call sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...), causing a NullPointerException. The test catches any RuntimeException and ignores it, so it would still pass even if the intended IllegalArgumentException path ("Unknown value ... for grant type") were removed, meaning the test is not exercising the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor null-checks grantType twice (copy-paste): the second Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') should check rawTokenId, which is never validated — a null rawTokenId slips through and encodeTokenId produces a jti ending in the literal string 'null'

adjudication.rationale: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java, the constructor null-checks grantType twice: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. This second check should validate `rawTokenId` but does not, so `rawTokenId` can be null. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, the return value concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which will yield the literal string "null" if rawTokenId is null, producing an invalid/undesired token id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor is a source/binary break: any out-of-tree grant implementation or test using new Context(existingContext) stops compiling/running

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (server-spi-private) by deleting the entire constructor body (lines ~97-118). Any external code that previously did `new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile, and binaries compiled against the old signature could fail with `NoSuchMethodError` if run against this version. This is a concrete API/binary compatibility concern introduced by the diff, though not necessarily an in-repo functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The remaining OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor now dereferences formParams.getFirst(...) (previously it only assigned the reference), so callers passing a null or late-populated formParams — previously tolerated, and the reason setFormParams exists — now NPE or capture a stale grantType if params are swapped later

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the constructor now immediately does `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` (OAuth2GrantType.java), which will NPE if `formParams` is null. Also, `setFormParams(...)` still exists but does not update `grantType`, so if callers replace/late-populate form params via `setFormParams`, `getGrantType()` can return a stale value inconsistent with the current `formParams`. Both issues are directly implied by the new field caching and lack of synchronization in the setter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wire-format break: initToken changes the jti of every access token from a UUID to 'xxxxxx:<uuid>' with no versioning/feature flag; external consumers that parsed jti as a UUID (dedup keys, DB column constraints, logging parsers, audit tooling) break for all newly issued tokens with no migration path

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes the access token `jti`/ID format for newly issued tokens: `TokenManager.initToken()` no longer sets `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` directly, but always prefixes encoded context and a colon via `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)` (e.g., `onrtcc:<rawId>`), and the new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` encodes as `6chars + ':' + rawTokenId`. There is no conditional/feature flag or versioning shown around this change, and tests were updated to expect the new format (`AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)`). This is a backward-compatibility/wire-format concern for external consumers that assumed UUID `jti`, but it is not an internal correctness defect demonstrated by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: initToken now unconditionally dereferences session.getContext().getClient() (via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken) with no null guard; extensions invoking TokenManager.createClientAccessToken/responseBuilder without setting the session context client now NPE and 500 on token issuance

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new unconditional call chain during access token creation: TokenManager.initToken() now always obtains a TokenContextEncoderProvider and calls DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...), which calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session). That method dereferences session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) with no null guard (and was changed to public static), so if session.getContext().getClient() is null on any token issuance path, this will NPE. The provider uses the session context client rather than the non-null ClientModel parameter passed into TokenManager.initToken, making the NPE risk plausible and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant paths that don't route through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse silently encode as 'na', leaving registered shortcuts unused: the GRANT_TYPE attribute is only set on the specific paths touched in this diff, so grants building token responses by another route (UMA's RPT response assembly, other token-exchange branches, custom TokenExchangeProviders) issue tokens labeled 'na' — silently, since the fallback is graceful and no test can detect the mislabel

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token ID generation to encode context including a grant-type shortcut (TokenManager.initToken now calls TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId based on clientSessionCtx). The encoder reads grant type solely from clientSessionContext attribute Constants.GRANT_TYPE and falls back to "na" when it’s missing (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext). This attribute is only set in a few specific paths touched here (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, TokenManager refresh validation, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider). Any other access-token issuance paths that call TokenManager.createClientAccessToken without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE will produce token IDs labeled "na" without warning. This is an incompleteness/coverage concern created by the change, not a proven runtime breakage from the diff alone.
